newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu takes Jerusalem battle to Arab street.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu takes Jerusalem battle to Arab street.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu took his battle over Jerusalem to the streets on Monday, touring the occupied Arab half of the city while Palestinians shut down to protest Israeli housing plans.

Netanyahu, trying to smother Arab anger at his plans to build 6,500 housing units for Jews in East Jerusalem, promised during a visit to the al-Thouri neighbourhood to upgrade infrastructure in the Arab half of the city.
"What we are doing today is making true to make Jerusalem one city for Jews and Arabs alike," Netanyahu said above a site where Israel has unloaded building materials for a sidewalk.
"We are serious about it. It's not a ploy. We're not playing games. We think that...it's our responsibility to treat its (Jerusalem's) Arab and Jewish residents alike."
Thouri, which straddles Jewish West Jerusalem, was shuttered by a general strike called to protest Israeli plans to build housing for Jews in Jerusalem's Jabal Abu Ghneim, also known as Har Homa.
Netanyahu enraged Palestinians and drew international criticism last week when his government approved a plan to start building 2,500 housing units in the first stage of construction of the project.

Israeli officials on Monday revealed that Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechi has begun pushing a plan to build 1,500 housing units for Jews and 3,000 hotel rooms that would link Maaleh Adumim settlement with Jewish enclaves north of the city.

Asked about the plan, Netanyahu said: "I haven't checked the bureaucratic procedures. But it's well known that we have plans to facilitate the development of Jerusalem for its Arab and Jewish residents alike."
The projects complete a circle of Jewish settlements around East Jerusalem which Israel began building after it captured the city from Jordan in the 1967 Middle East war.

The Israeli moves came just weeks before Israel and the PLO are due to resume negotiations on a permanent peace settlement, which under the broad 1993 self-rule deal must include talks on the future of Jerusalem.
Israel regards Jerusalem, including the Arab half, as its eternal capital. The PLO wants East Jerusalem to be the capital of a future Palestinian state.
Palestinians shut their businesses, schools and government offices heeding a call by the Palestinian Legislative Council to protest against the Israeli construction plans.

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, in Washington on an official visit, was expected to ask President Bill Clinton to pressure Israel to cancel the construction plans when the two meet later on Monday.
Arafat on Saturday accused Netanyahu of trying to destroy the peace process.
"This settlement issue is an attempt by Israel to blast to smithereens the peace process," Arafat told an emergency meeting of the Arab League in Cairo.
He said that under self-rule deals signed with late prime minister Yitzhak Rabin, Israel was to halt construction of any housing units in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
Arafat warned he might declare the establishment of an independent Palestinian state in response to Netanyahu's moves.
Netanyahu responded by saying Arafat would bring peace moves to a halt if he unilaterally declared a Palestinian state now.

"And if someone wants to declare, today, the establishment of a Palestinian state, let him do it. It will be a serious mistake, a severe mistake, that will bring a halt to the entire process," Netanyahu told members of his Likud party in Tel Aviv on Sunday.
